summary: Warren Cove range lights: two 1907 wooden towers on Charlottetown Harbour, PEI, kept in line to guide ships to the wharves. Both are listed as active.

structures.note: Lighthouse Society: 11.2 m (37 ft) from base to vane, focal height 17.3 m. The 1907 report gives 30 ft (9.1 m) from base to ventilator. Rowlett gives 7.5 m (25 ft). The record gives 11.0 m.
Lighthouse Society: 7.7 m (25 ft 2 in) tower, focal height 21.4 m (70 ft 2 in). Rowlett gives 7.5 m (25 ft) and focal plane 23 m (76 ft).

access.note: Grounds open, towers closed. Both lights are on the grounds of the Fort Amherst-Port La Joye National Historic Site, reached from the site's interpretive centre (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Society).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (Lighthouse Friends); Government of Canada (Lighthouse Society)

events.note: Established as range lights; fixed red seventh-order dioptric lights, visible 2 miles in the line of range (1907 report)
Built by M. Walsh to a Department design, framed at the Government Wharf warehouse, Charlottetown

1908 report: range lights that last year's report had stated to be under construction were completed in the year to 31 March 1908, cost complete $326.64. The reports do not agree on the stage of the work.
Renamed from Warren Farm to Warren Cove in the early 1960s; the exact year is not given
Towers repaired after a rot investigation; plywood and Nailite siding; flared cornice made angled; original colours kept on the rear light

notes_for_editor: Disagreements left in the story: (1) the 1907 report says the range was established; the 1908 report says the range that last year's report stated to be under construction was completed in fiscal 1908 (fiscal years end 31 March). (2) Heights: 1907 report 30 ft per tower; Lighthouse Society 37 ft front and 25 ft rear; Rowlett 25 ft for both; the record has 11.0 m for the front. (3) Focal heights: Society 17.3 m and 21.4 m; Rowlett 17 m and 23 m. (4) Colour: red in 1907 and 1908; yellow in later sources; the change is undated. (5) Owner: Lighthouse Friends says the Canadian Coast Guard; the Lighthouse Society says the Government of Canada and that a group seeks ownership through Parks Canada's Heritage Lighthouse Program. The record's agency Parks Canada comes from Wikidata and is not cited. (6) Cost: the 1907 report's OCR reads $1,295.39 for the work to date; the Lighthouse Society and Lighthouse Friends give $1,495.39 for both lights. The figure is left out of the story. Check the page image at scan p. 39 before any cost is published. (7) The 1914 Newson line is matched by column position in the OCR (scan p. 69); check the image. (8) The 1910 Block House and Warren Farm rows are on the same printed page (p. 253); the OCR prints Warren Farm as 'Warren Fann Range'. (9) Keepers after 1921 (Feehan, Grovette, White, MacKinnon) come from Lighthouse Friends only. A search of the Canadian statements in the corpus for 1916 to 1924 found no Warren Farm entry, so these names are unconfirmed. (10) No storms, wrecks or rescues are sourced for this station; that chapter is omitted. (11) Wikipedia (English and French) and Wikidata were read for leads only and are not cited. (12) Newspapers were not searched; the station's Charlottetown papers are not in Chronicling America. (13) Possible corrections: none confirmed. The record's front height 11.0 m is within the range of sources and was not proposed as a correction. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1907 entry is in the Chief Engineer's report for the nine months ending 31 March 1907 (not a fiscal-year report); the 1908 entry is in the fiscal year ending 31 March 1908. The 1914 Newson row and the 1910 McNeil rows were read on the archive.org page images: Newson sits on the same printed row as Warren farm range, and the 1910 Warren Fann row reads 100 00 salary on the same row as McNeil. The $326.64 cost (1908) is read from OCR and was not checked against the image. The 1907 cost (OCR $1,295.39; LF and Society $1,495.39) stays out of the story.
